newsitem.title: UK: Excerpts from UK PM John Major's speech.
newsitem.headline: Excerpts from UK PM John Major's speech.

text.p: Following are excerpts from British Prime Minister John Major's speech to the UK Conservative party's annual conference:
- Major repeated Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's pledge to introduce a 20 percent basic tax rate for everyone when this was affordable. "That's our priority."
- "We know that cutting taxes isn't government giving anything back to people. It's the government taking away less of people's own money. That's why low taxes are right."
- Major said that in order to encourage wealth creation for the future, the Conservatives would reduce and then abolish capital gains tax.
- "We don't want to soak the taxpayer. Labour often say they want to soak the rich. But they're the only party in history who also regularly manage to soak the poor."
- "Over time, our next target is to remove the burden of inheritance tax. Building wealth for the many, not the few."

- "Unlike Labour, we aren't ashamed of our past. Unlike Labour, we haven't abandoned our principles. Unlike Labour, we haven't had to reinvent ourselves. We are proud of what we've achieved. Because we've changed Britain for the better."

- "When I became Prime Minister, I set out to make Britain a low inflation economy. I knew what a fight it would be. But we went for it.... We did what we always do when we're challenged: we came out fighting. And as a result, we've had the longest run of low inflation this country has seen for a generation."

- "Between us, we've transformed the prospects for the future of the country we love....We set out to create jobs - and we're succeeding. Unemployment is lower here than in any comparable country in Europe. In Britain it's falling. In Europe it's not."
- Major said the UK was set for higher growth last year, this year and next year than any major country in Europe.

- "The plain truth is I'm the first Prime Minister for generations who can say: 'we're the most competitive economy in Europe'. And I intend to be the Prime Minister who builds on that success after we've won the next general election."
- Major said the central question at the election would be: who can be trusted with the future?

- "Labour try to persuade people it's them...Trouble is they're wrong in the present as well. And it simply won't do for be Prime Minister please?'. Sorry Tony. Job's taken. And anyway, it's too big a task for your first real job."
- "Giving people opportunity marks the great divide in British politics...Our belief in choice is the driving force of our policy."
- On education, Major said "Our task is to provide a rich choice of schools and colleges, giving the best to every child and demanding the best of every child."
- "We're improving that choice every year and we intend to widen it further...This autumn...we'll turn today's promises into tomorrow's reality with a flagship Education Bill."
- Major said the Conservatives had "cut direct tax, given more and more people the opportunity to save, to own shares, own pensions, own homes."

- "In our next five years, we will seek new opportunities; an opportunity owning democracy. Helping more people save and build security for retirement. Helping people who need care keep more of those savings."
- "We're aiming for the least possible tax to give the greatest possible choice. As we can afford it, we'll move to a 20 pence basic rate for all. That's our priority.

- "I can't stand welfare cheats...We're determined that taxpayers' money goes where it's needed. Our task is to build a welfare system for the 21st century. A system for a self-help society - not a help-yourself society. And one way of building independence is to get more people back to work."

- "The minimum wage is the wage of the dole queue. It's not a wage at all. How can you talk of a Social Chapter that makes it more difficult for people to find work. That's why I say they're no-go areas for jobs and no-go areas for us."
- "Last year I announced our plans to develop a Contract for Work. This week we Tories took a big step forward with the start of our new Jobseekers Allowance."
- The Prime Minister pledged to help those who had been out of work the longest. "First, we give them help to find a job and if that doesn't succeed, they'll be offered work on a community project."

- On the National Health Service, Major said: "Our NHS is unique. In this country, when you're ill, we take your temperature. In other countries, they take your credit card. While I'm in Downing Street, that will never happen here. That doesn't mean the National Health Service shouldn't change. It must."

- On Europe, Major said: "Some of our partners do see the future of Europe as ever-closer political as well as economic integration. We don't believe this is practical, nor, to be frank, desirable. It's not the Europe we joined and it's not a Europe we can accept."
- "Europe must become more flexible and responsive...the only realistic future is as a partnership of nations."
